title: 5 Signs Your Account Has Been Hacked (and What to Do First)
excerpt: Most people find out their account is compromised too late. Learn the early warning signs, and the exact first moves that save your account.
body:
After recovering 20+ stolen accounts, I can tell you the victims all said the same thing: "I noticed something small and ignored it." Here's what to look for, and what to do the moment you see it.

1. You received a "login from a new device" alert you don't recognise

This is the classic first warning. Even if it looks like a spam email, don't click anything inside it, go directly to the platform's security page yourself and check recent activity.

2. Friends say they got strange messages "from you"

DMs asking for money, codes or urgent help are the #1 sign someone is inside your account. Your contacts are their next victims.

3. Your password "stopped working"

If your password suddenly fails and your recovery email or phone has been changed, the attacker has locked you out. Act immediately, most platforms have a short window where recovery is easiest.

4. Settings you didn't change

Unknown forwarding addresses, linked apps, a new phone number, or an email you don't recognise in your security settings. Attackers add these as back doors.

5. You can't see your sent messages or archived content

Sometimes attackers hide their tracks by deleting or archiving. If folders look rearranged, investigate.

Speed is everything. The first hour after you notice is when the account is most recoverable.

What to do first, in order

  • Change the password from a device the hacker has never used
  • Log out of all sessions in security settings
  • Turn on two step verification
  • Revoke unknown third party apps
  • Alert your contacts so they don't fall for messages "from you"

If it's already too far gone, don't panic, I help victims of scams and recover hacked or stolen accounts. Reach out, the earlier the better.
